title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
summary: Design a class that reports the kth largest value seen so far every time a new number arrives.

tests.explain: k = 3. After adding 5 the values are 9, 7, 5, 4, 1, so the 3rd largest is 5. Adding 2 changes nothing at the top. After 8 the top three are 9, 8, 7; after 10 they are 10, 9, 8; 6 is too small to enter.
With k = 1 the answer is simply the largest value so far. The class starts empty; duplicates count, so the second 0 keeps the answer at 0.
The constructor gets fewer than k values. After adding 3 there are exactly two (5 and 3), so the 2nd largest is 3. Then 8 arrives: the top two are 8 and 5.

hints: Values below the kth largest can never become the answer again: new values only push the kth largest up. How many values do you really need to keep?
Keep just the k largest values in a min-heap. The heap's top, its smallest element, is then exactly the kth largest of everything seen.
In add, push the value, and if the heap now holds more than k values, pop once. Return the top. Feed the constructor's nums through the same steps.

complexity.time: O(log k) per add, and O(n log k) to load the n starting values
complexity.space: O(k): the heap never holds more than k values
